summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease who recently transitioned to peritoneal dialysis was admitted with acute abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. He was diagnosed with peritonitis based on elevated peritoneal fluid white blood cells (530) with no organism identified on culture or gram stain. He was treated with intraperitoneal ceftazidime after an initial dose of IV vancomycin and ceftriaxone, with rapid improvement in symptoms. Vancomycin was discontinued due to a high trough level. The patient responded well, with resolution of pain and stable labs. His wife expressed difficulty managing peritoneal dialysis at home, prompting discussion about returning to hemodialysis. He was discharged home on continued intraperitoneal antibiotics for three weeks with close nephrology follow-up.
problems: Infection following other infusion, injection, transfusion, or vaccination
